div.l: He hadde of gold ywrought a ful curious pynne
A loue knotte in the gretter ende ther was
His heued was balled / that shon as eny glas
And eek his face / as he hadde ben anoynt
He was a lord ful fat and in good poynt
His eyen stepe and / rolled in his hede
That stremed as a furneys of lede
His botes souple his hors in grete astate
Now certeinly he was a faire prelate
He nas not pale as a forpyned gost
A fat swan loued he best of eny rost
His palfrey was as broıı̄un as a berye
A Frere ther was a wantoıı̄un and a merye
A lymitour a ful solempne man
In alle the ordres foure / is ther nouȝt oon that can
So moche of daliance / and faire langage
He hadde maad ful many a mariage
Of ȝonge women at his owene cost
Vn to his ordre he was a noble post
Ful wel biloued and famuler was he
Wᵗith frankeleynes oủre al in his cuntre
And with worthy women of the toıı̄un
For he hadde power of confessioıı̄un
As seide hym self more than a curat
For of his ordre he was licenciat
Ful swetely herde he confessioıı̄un
And plesant was his absolucioıı̄un
He was an esy man to ȝeue penaıı̄unce
¶ There as he wiste to haue a good pitance
For vnto a poủere ordre for to ȝeue
Is signe that a man is wel yshryue
For ȝif he ȝaf he dorste make auaunt
He wiste that a man was repentant
For many a man so hard is of his herte
He may nought wepe / al though hym sore smerte
Therfore in stede of wepyng and prayeres
Men muste ȝeue siluer / to the pouere freres
His typet was ay farsed ful of knyves
And pynnes for to ȝeue faire wyues
